overview: This file assembles U.S. consular reporting on population statistics for the Japanese-administered Kwantung Leased Territory and the South Manchuria Railway Zone between 1931 and 1938. Cabot Coville’s 1931 despatch transmits detailed tables derived from the census of October 1, 1930, covering population by locality, sex, nationality or race, housing, density, and changes since 1920 and 1925. A 1938 report by William T. Turner updates the leased territory’s population to 1,190,003 at the end of 1937 and lists figures for its principal urban centers. Subsequent correspondence investigates striking discrepancies with the Manchuria Yearbook and establishes that, except for an enlarged Dairen, the reported urban figures mistakenly represented broader police supervisory districts rather than the cities themselves.

subfiles.title: Despatch from Coville on the 1930 Kwantung and railway-zone census
subfiles.from: Cabot Coville, American Vice Consul, Dairen
subfiles.about: The despatch transmits two tabulations compiled from the October 1, 1930 census of the Kwantung Leased Territory and South Manchuria Railway Zone.
subfiles.summary: Coville reports that the Kwantung Leased Territory’s population rose 24.8 percent between 1925 and 1930 to nearly one million, with Chinese residents continuing to form seven-eighths of the population. He comments on the territory’s exceptionally high density and on the sex imbalance among its Chinese and Japanese populations. The South Manchuria Railway Zone grew by 29.1 percent to nearly 400,000, with a rising Chinese share and a still-pronounced excess of Chinese men.

subfiles.title: Enclosure: 1930 census of the Kwantung Leased Territory and South Manchuria Railway Zone
subfiles.from: American Consulate, Dairen, compiled from Kwantung Government census returns
subfiles.about: This enclosure tabulates the October 1930 census by territorial subdivision and railway-zone locality.
subfiles.summary: The table covers the leased territory’s principal districts and fourteen South Manchuria Railway Zone localities. It supplies area, dwellings, population totals by sex, nationality or race, density, persons per dwelling, male-to-female ratios, and population change since 1920 and 1925. The figures permit comparisons among Dairen, Port Arthur, Jinzhou, Pulandian, Pikou, and railway cities extending from southern Manchuria to Changchun.

subfiles.title: Enclosure: Comparative table of the 1930 census
subfiles.from: American Consulate, Dairen, compiled from Kwantung Government census returns
subfiles.about: This enclosure compares aggregate census statistics for 1920, 1925, and 1930 and calculates changes over the intervening periods.
subfiles.summary: The table separates totals for the Kwantung Leased Territory and South Manchuria Railway Zone and compares their area, dwellings, population, sex distribution, and nationality or race. It also presents absolute increases between 1925 and 1930 and between 1920 and 1930. The table documents rapid demographic expansion and changing composition across the Japanese-administered areas.

subfiles.title: Turner report on the population of the Kwantung Leased Territory
subfiles.from: William T. Turner, American Consul, Dairen
subfiles.to: Commercial Office, U.S. Department of State
subfiles.about: The report presents the leased territory’s population at the end of December 1937 by sex, nationality or race, and principal urban center.
subfiles.summary: Turner reports a total population of 1,190,003, an increase of 41,969 over 1936, with males exceeding females by 172,393. He divides the population into 1,009,870 Chinese, 174,587 Japanese, 3,917 Koreans, and 1,629 other foreigners. The report also gives large figures for Dairen, Port Arthur, Pulandian, Pikou, and Jinzhou that later correspondence reveals were, except for Dairen, figures for broader police supervisory areas.

subfiles.title: Department instruction requesting clarification of city population figures
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, Dairen
subfiles.about: The Department asks the Dairen consulate to reconcile its population figures with much smaller figures in the 1938 Japanese-language Manchuria Yearbook.
subfiles.summary: The instruction compares the five urban figures reported on February 26 with those printed in the Manchuria Yearbook. It observes that the consular figures correspond more closely to the Yearbook’s populations for districts bearing the cities’ names than to the cities themselves. The consular officer is therefore directed to investigate and submit a further report.

subfiles.title: Turner despatch correcting the city population figures
subfiles.from: William T. Turner, American Consul, Dairen
subfiles.about: Turner explains the discrepancy in the 1937 urban statistics and supplies corrected figures for four cities.
subfiles.summary: Turner identifies the Department’s source as the Manshū Nenkan and explains that its Dairen figure dated from July 1937, before several suburbs were incorporated into the city. Kwantung Government authorities confirmed that the enlarged city had 503,778 inhabitants in December 1937. Turner acknowledges that the earlier report mistakenly placed the populations of police supervisory areas under city headings and corrects the figures to Port Arthur 31,439, Jinzhou 21,473, Pulandian 21,320, and Pikou 19,780.

interest: The file is valuable for reconstructing demographic change in Japan’s Kwantung leasehold and along the South Manchuria Railway immediately before the establishment of Manchukuo and again during the late 1930s. Its detailed tables expose striking population growth, ethnic composition, migration-related sex imbalances, and sharp differences among urban and railway settlements. Especially useful is the 1938 exchange: it documents how incompatible administrative units—cities versus police supervisory districts—and changing municipal boundaries could produce major statistical errors, while also showing the State Department’s process for detecting and correcting them.
